topic: Deterministic–randomized honest-interval frontier for sparse staggered Poisson proportional effects. Fix T at least 3, alpha in (0,.1), observed cohort shares bounded below, and exact independent cohort-time Poisson totals with intensity kappa, normalized time effects, bounded positive exposure masses, and treated multipliers in [1/2,3]. The target is the counterfactual-share weighted proportional effect in [-1/2,2]. Define worst-nuisance minimax expected-length functions for deterministic connected intervals and randomized interval kernels measurable from shares and counts. Prove the exact low-intensity deterministic value, characterize every optimizer and least-favorable configuration, establish the strict randomized gap, and keep the all-untreated-zero restriction as a separate comparison. For arbitrary compact intensity ranges, construct finite count-box and endpoint-grid mixed-integer primal certificates with matching integer lower witnesses and outward error bounds; derive the high-intensity efficient-Gaussian minimax bridge. Credit Moreau–Kastler for the imputed PTT workflow, Martin and Wooldridge for regular fixed-T inference, and generic weak-ratio theory. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Independent derivations recovered the three intensity extrema, exact small-intensity deterministic values, observed-share optimizer allowances, randomized zero-information limit, all-intensity zero-atom lower bound, finite integer witness property, and fixed-design Poisson polynomial separation. Arithmetic checks covered T=3 through 12, untreated-zero versus denominator-zero events, integrality gaps, endpoint contacts, count tails, and Gaussian variance examples; no exact collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove an effective finite covering of the observed-share simplex by uniformly honest finite-grid policy regions, including nominal-coverage contacts, target-endpoint strata, compact intensity variation, and matching integer lower certificates with the full error budget. EARLY KILL TEST: At T=3, alpha=.05, intensity=.01, reproduce the small-count witness and certify a globally honest observed-share deterministic primal and integer lower certificate within .05 using count box K=2 and endpoint mesh .01; any relaxation, sampled-grid check, or fixed-share-only certificate fails. open_problems.open_problem: Construct an effective finite certification theorem for globally honest connected-interval policies over compact Poisson-intensity ranges and the full observed-share simplex, using finite count boxes and endpoint grids with matching mixed-integer primal and integer lower certificates.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing computational minimax work supplies convergent finite approximations, while exact Poisson interval constructions exploit a one-dimensional ordered family. Neither gives deterministic, auditable upper and lower certificates uniform over observed shares, normalized multiplicative nuisance parameters, target boundaries, and intensity. The prior rare-event proposal likewise establishes only a finite abstract profile and explicitly leaves continuous-profile transfer open; the PT-All review shows that strict inequalities or distance-to-null shortcuts fail at nonclosed boundary contacts. The missing proof step is a contact-stratified finite covering with analytic Poisson-tail truncation, uniform cellwise coverage moduli, separate treatment of nominal-coverage and target-endpoint strata, and a complete outward error budget that preserves an integer lower witness.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For every compact intensity range and tolerance ε, a finite contact-stratified covering theorem with explicit count-tail, endpoint-mesh, intensity-mesh, share-cell, and numerical-rounding errors, together with an outward-rounded globally honest mixed-integer policy and an integer lower witness bracketing the continuum minimax value within ε.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing keeps the certification problem tied to the counterfactual-share-weighted proportional estimand and makes uniformity over observed cohort shares substantively necessary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Nonlinear staggered DiD requires counterfactual-share aggregation -> sparse Poisson totals require exact rather than Gaussian calibration -> the nuisance and observed-share domains remain continuous despite countable observations -> finite policies need certified continuum honesty at every contact stratum.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the finite-support least-favorable-prior game and likelihood-ratio inversion, replacing asymptotic simulation convergence by deterministic discretization bounds and a certified primal-lower-witness gap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems optimize honest expected-size procedures over compact multidimensional parameter spaces; the desired resolution strengthens approximation into an explicit continuum certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over exact enumeration of discrete acceptance regions and monotone endpoint control, then replace the scalar ordering argument with uniform multivariate Poisson tail and cellwise coverage bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its construction is an exact finite-count prototype, while the destination requires many count coordinates and continuous nuisance, intensity, and share variation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use drifting-sequence and subsequence arguments to prove uniform size at boundary and contact configurations where pointwise approximations fail.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The covering theorem must control sequences approaching nominal-coverage and target-endpoint contacts, precisely where sampled-grid validity does not imply global honesty.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the exact low-intensity worst-nuisance minimax expected length for deterministic connected intervals for counterfactual-share-weighted staggered-Poisson proportional effects, characterize every optimizer and least-favorable configuration, and establish whether randomized interval kernels attain a strictly smaller value.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The staggered-PPML literature supplies identification and regular large-sample estimation, while exact-discrete interval papers treat scalar binomial or Poisson parameters and explicit minimax solutions concern simpler experiment families. The prior rare-event run proves only a nonshrinking bounded-count lower obstruction, and the platform run's interval-kernel construction concerns a known-randomization finite-population experiment. The first transfer step that fails is reduction to a monotone scalar sufficient statistic: the causal target is a bounded ratio-like functional of several independent cohort-time Poisson means with normalized time effects, observed-share-dependent weights, exposure masses, and multidimensional nuisance parameters. No located source compares deterministic connected interval maps with their randomized-kernel convexification in this staggered causal experiment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Exact low-κ formulas for deterministic and randomized minimax expected-length functions, necessary-and-sufficient descriptions of all optimal policies and least-favorable nuisance/share configurations, and a regime theorem establishing a strict randomized improvement.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative moves from staggered adoption and nonlinear outcomes to a precisely weighted proportional estimand, providing the natural setup before sparse-count inferential failure is introduced.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Staggered treatment invalidates naive aggregation -> multiplicative outcomes require a counterfactual-share-weighted proportional estimand -> sparse Poisson totals make regular PPML intervals nonuniform -> determine the exact deterministic-randomized honest-interval frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over Bayes-minimax duality and inversion of level-α tests against least-favorable alternatives, replacing the restricted-location likelihood by the finite multivariate Poisson likelihood.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested object is an honest confidence procedure minimizing maximum expected length for a bounded parameter, but now in a discrete panel experiment with a causal functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt auxiliary-uniform probability-atom splitting and prove strict expected-length improvement through test inversion and slack removal at discrete coverage contacts.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Discreteness is the structural source of the proposed deterministic-randomized gap; the new argument must extend scalar ordered atom splitting to a multivariate Poisson nuisance game.

method_exemplars.technique: Impute untreated counterfactual means under multiplicative time effects and aggregate treated and counterfactual masses into the proportional target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies the causal target map whose exact finite-count sampling experiment is being optimized.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Regular PPML theory establishes pointwise asymptotic normality or diagnoses incidental-parameter bias, but it does not prove convergence of the worst-nuisance expected-length game or track boundary strata of the bounded proportional target. General Poisson-Gaussian equivalence results concern different experiment classes and do not identify the efficient gradient after time-effect normalization and counterfactual-share weighting. The prior cycle-efficiency run derives a canonical gradient and an attaining fixed-T estimator but explicitly stops at pointwise asymptotic linearity; another reviewer flags the absence of a valid full-ball LAN argument. The missing first step is a uniform LAN or two-sided Le Cam comparison after nuisance profiling that preserves observed-share variation, target boundaries, connected-interval loss, and minimax test inversion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform LAN or Le Cam comparison theorem for the normalized cohort-time Poisson experiment, an explicit efficient influence vector, variance, and least-favorable submodel for the proportional target, and matching upper and lower expansions showing that the scaled deterministic and randomized minimax lengths converge to the bounded-Gaussian minimax value.

writing_exemplar.why: Its setup moves cleanly from nonlinear parallel trends to pooled Poisson estimation and regular standard errors, furnishing the high-information endpoint the exact bridge should recover.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Count outcomes motivate nonlinear parallel trends -> pooled Poisson QMLE gives regular fixed-T inference at high information -> sparse exact honesty need not resemble Wald inference -> establish when the exact minimax problem converges to the efficient Gaussian benchmark.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt explicit Poisson-to-Gaussian randomizations and two-sided deficiency bounds to the finite independent-count likelihood, then compose the comparison with the causal target map and confidence-set loss.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested bridge is a decision-theoretic transfer of honest-interval risk from a Poisson experiment to a Gaussian experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the bounded-normal minimax expected-length characterization and its least-favorable dual as the limiting confidence-interval game.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After efficient nuisance projection, the target is bounded and locally Gaussian, matching the restricted-location confidence-set geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Profile multiplicative untreated means and aggregate imputed counterfactual masses into the counterfactual-share-weighted proportional effect.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The limit experiment and efficient gradient must preserve the exact causal target and its normalization.

literature_map:
Moreau-Kastler (2025, EU Tax Observatory WP31, SSRN 5247936) supplies the closest estimand: a counterfactual-share-weighted proportional effect for staggered PPML and identifies nonlinear aggregation as the central obstacle.
Wooldridge (2023, Econometrics Journal, 10.1093/ectj/utad016) identifies cohort-time effects under nonlinear or index parallel trends and develops pooled Poisson QMLE with regular large-sample inference.
Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024, Review of Economic Studies, arXiv:2108.12419) give the linear staggered-DiD imputation and efficiency template transported toward proportional effects.
Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1803.09015) establish group-time identification, aggregation, and simultaneous inference for staggered DiD in an additive-effect framework.
Sun and Abraham (2021, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1804.05785) establish contamination of conventional event-study coefficients under heterogeneous effects, motivating cohort-time targets.
Weidner and Zylkin (2021, Journal of International Economics, arXiv:1909.01327) show that fixed-T PPML consistency can coexist with biased conventional centering and variance estimation in multiway panels.
Kabaila and Byrne (2001, Canadian Journal of Statistics, 10.2307/3316053) provide an exact short interval and computable monotone-endpoint construction for one Poisson mean.
Habiger, McCann, and Tebbs (2013, Statistics & Probability Letters, 10.1016/j.spl.2012.09.018) optimize nonrandomized intervals for one-parameter discrete families, including Poisson models.
Kabaila (2013, arXiv:1302.6659) isolates probability-atom splitting as a source of strict randomized improvement in a scalar discrete confidence-interval problem.
Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005, Bernoulli, 10.3150/bj/1126126761) formulate minimax expected-measure confidence sets through test inversion and Bayes-minimax duality.
Schafer and Stark (2009, JASA, 10.1198/jasa.2009.tm07420) approximate minimax expected-size confidence regions on compact spaces using finite-support prior games, but do not provide the requested deterministic continuum certificate.
Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang (2004, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:math/0503674) establish Poisson-Gaussian experiment equivalence, supplying machinery for a high-intensity bridge.
The central tension is between exact discrete honesty with multidimensional nuisance parameters and regular fixed-T PPML inference; no located paper joins that tension to worst-nuisance expected length for the counterfactual-share-weighted staggered-Poisson target.
The scan also found no occupied target-method pair for globally certified mixed-integer interval policies over observed-share simplices or for a deterministic-versus-randomized minimax frontier in this causal panel experiment.
